source_text: Idcirco et m columba uenit Spiritus sanctus: simplex animal et laetum est, non felle amarum, non morsibus saeuum, non unguium laceratione uiolentum, hospitia humana diligere, unius domus consortium nosse, cum generant simul filios edere, cum commeant uolatibus inuicem cohaerere, communi conuersatione uitam suam degere, oris osculo concordiam pacis agnoscere, legem circa omnia unanimitatis inplere. haec est in ecclesia noscenda simplicitas, haec caritas obtinenda, ut columbas dilectio fiaternitat imitetur, ut mansuetudo et lenitas agnis et ouibus aequetur. quid facit in pectore christiano luporum feritas et canum rabies et uenenum letale serpentum et cruenta saeuitia bestiarum? gratulandum est, cum tales de ecclesia separantur, ne columbas, ne oues Christi saeua sua et uenenata contagione praedentur. cohaerere et coniungi non potest amaritudo cum dulcedine, caligo cum lumine, pluuia cum serenitate, pugna cum pace, cum fecunditate sterilitas, cum fontibus siccitas, cum tranquillitate tempestas. nemo existimet bonos de ecclesia posse discedere: triticum non rapit uentus nec arborem solida radice fundatam procella subuertit: inanes paleae tempestate iactantur, inualidae arbores turbinis incursione uertuntur. hos execratur et percutit Iohannes apostolus dicens: ex nobis exierunt, sed non [fuerunt ex nobis. si enim fuissent ex nobis, mansissent nobiscum.
thought_title: The Dove's Simplicity and the Separation of the Wicked
orientation: Cyprian is explaining how the Holy Spirit's descent as a dove reveals the simplicity and unity that must mark the Church, and why the departure of the wicked is cause for rejoicing.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore also the Holy Spirit came as a dove: it is a simple and joyful animal, not bitter with gall, not fierce with bites, not violent with tearing of claws, to love human dwellings, to know the partnership of one house, when they breed to bring forth offspring together, when they travel to cling to one another in flight, to pass their life in shared converse, to recognize the harmony of peace with the kiss of the beak, to fulfill the law of unanimity in all things. This simplicity is to be recognized in the Church, this love is to be maintained, so that love may imitate doves for the brotherhood, so that gentleness and mildness may be made equal to lambs and sheep. What does the savagery of wolves and the madness of dogs and the deadly venom of serpents and the bloody cruelty of beasts do in a Christian breast? It is to be rejoiced when such people are separated from the Church, lest they prey upon the doves, lest they prey upon the sheep of Christ with their savage and venomous contagion. Bitterness cannot cling and be joined with sweetness, darkness with light, rain with fair weather, battle with peace, barrenness with fruitfulness, dryness with springs, storm with calm. Let no one think that the good can depart from the Church: the wind does not carry off the wheat, nor does the gale overturn a tree founded on a solid root: empty chaff is tossed by the storm, weak trees are overturned by the onset of the whirlwind. The apostle John curses and strikes these, saying: they went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have remained with us.

lemmas.gloss: they travel, go to and fro

choices.english: when they breed to bring forth offspring together
choices.why: The clause describes doves' shared parental behavior: when they breed, they together bring forth their young. 'Simul' modifies the joint action of producing offspring, not the timing of eating.
rejected: when they give birth they eat together
when they beget they eat their young together

choices.english: to recognize the harmony of peace with the kiss of the beak
choices.why: 'Oris osculo' is literally 'with the kiss of the mouth/beak'; rendering 'beak' clarifies the dove imagery while keeping the literal sense of the body part.
rejected: with the kiss of the mouth

choices.english: this love is to be maintained
choices.why: 'Obtinenda' is a gerundive expressing necessity; 'maintained' captures the sense of holding fast to love, consistent with the glossary rendering of 'caritas' as 'love'.
rejected: this charity is to be held

choices.english: so that love may imitate doves for the brotherhood
choices.why: The Latin is awkward ('fiaternitat' is a misspelling of 'fraternitatem'); the sense is that love should imitate the doves' behavior toward the brotherhood. 'For the brotherhood' preserves the dative/accusative ambiguity without over-interpreting.
rejected: so that love of the brotherhood may imitate doves
so that brotherly love may imitate doves

choices.term: hos execratur et percutit Iohannes apostolus
choices.english: The apostle John curses and strikes these
choices.why: 'Execratur' means to curse or execrate; 'percutit' means to strike or smite. Both verbs are active and forceful, matching Cyprian's polemical tone against schismatics.
rejected: John the apostle execrates and rebukes these
these the apostle John curses and refutes

bible_refs.note: ex nobis exierunt, sed non fuerunt ex nobis. si enim fuissent ex nobis, mansissent nobiscum

pass_b_english: That is why the Holy Spirit came as a dove: a simple and joyful creature, not bitter with gall, not fierce with bites, not violent with tearing claws. It loves human dwellings, knows the sharing of one house, and when they have young they eat together. When they travel in flight they cling to one another, they pass their life in common company, they recognize the harmony of peace with the kiss of the beak, and they fulfill the law of unanimity in all things. This is the simplicity to be recognized in the Church; this is the love to be maintained, so that the love of the brotherhood may imitate doves, so that gentleness and mildness may equal lambs and sheep. What place does the ferocity of wolves, the madness of dogs, the deadly venom of serpents, and the bloody savagery of beasts have in a Christian heart? We should rejoice when such people are separated from the Church, so that they do not prey upon the doves and sheep of Christ with their savage and poisonous contagion. Bitterness cannot cling and be joined to sweetness, darkness to light, rain to fair weather, battle to peace, barrenness to fruitfulness, dryness to springs, storm to calm. Let no one think that the good can depart from the Church: the wind does not carry away the wheat, nor does a gale overturn a tree founded on a solid root. Empty chaff is tossed by the storm; weak trees are overturned by the blast of the whirlwind. The apostle John curses and strikes these, saying: "They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have remained with us" (1 John 2:19).
notes: The source has 'm columba' where 'm' appears to be a typographical error or abbreviation for 'in' (in columba), as the sense requires 'as a dove' or 'in the form of a dove'. The gloss renders the intended sense.
The source has 'fiaternitat' which is a misspelling of 'fraternitatem' (brotherhood).

problems.quote: so that love may imitate doves for the brotherhood
problems.why: The Latin means 'so that the love of the brotherhood may imitate doves,' not 'love may imitate doves for the brotherhood'; agency is reversed.
problems.fix: so that the love of the brotherhood may imitate doves

problems.quote: when they breed they bring forth their young together
problems.why: 'edere' means to eat, not to bring forth; doves eat together when they have young, a sign of shared life.
problems.fix: when they have young they eat together
problems.ruling: 'edere' = to eat; 'bring forth' = edere/gignere. Doves eat young together, not 'bring forth' them.

edits.new: so that the love of the brotherhood may imitate doves

Corrected 'when they breed they bring forth their young together' to 'when they have young they eat together' (source: 'cum generant simul filios edere').

last_rejected.quote: The apostle John curses and strikes these, saying
last_rejected.source_quote: hos execratur et percutit Iohannes apostolus dicens
last_rejected.why: English hides that John is the one cursed/struck, not the one doing it.
last_rejected.fix: These John the apostle curses and strikes, saying
last_rejected.ruling: 'Iohannes apostolus' is nominative subject of 'execratur et percutit'; John does the cursing. English is correct.

last_rejected.quote: when they have young they eat together
last_rejected.why: Latin says parents eat with their young, not 'they' ambiguously; 'cum generant' = when they give birth.
last_rejected.fix: and when they give birth, they eat with their young
last_rejected.ruling: 'cum generant simul filios edere' = when they bear young, to feed [them] together; English 'they have young they eat together' captures the sense adequately.
